After Kd8, White has many checks but Black is winning because after any of White's forcing moves, Black will capture the undefended b2 pawn with extra material. The position is decisively winning for Black.

**Best move:** Nxd3

**Main line:** Nxd3 Qxf7+ Kd8 (and Black is winning with the extra pawn and centralized knight)

**Motif:** hangingPiece

**Explanation:**
White's d3 pawn is undefended and attacked by your knight—a classic loose piece target. After you capture Nxd3, your knight cannot be recaptured immediately. When White tries Qxf7+ to create complications, your king moves (say Kd8) and you escape with an extra pawn while your knight dominates from d3. The lesson: always scan for undefended pieces, especially when your piece can grab one with tempo or without losing material.
